questions.enonce_markdown: State the differences between aerobic and anaerobic respiration. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Aerobic respiration | Anaerobic respiration |
|---|---|
| Needs **free oxygen**. | Takes place **without oxygen**. |
| Glucose is **completely oxidised**. | Glucose is **only partly broken down**. |
| Products: **carbon dioxide and water**. | Products: **ethanol (alcohol) and carbon dioxide** in yeast and plants, or **lactic acid** in animal muscles. |
| Releases a **large amount of energy** (about 2900 kJ per mole of glucose). | Releases **little energy** (about 210 kJ per mole of glucose). |
| Occurs in the **mitochondria** (and cytoplasm). | Occurs in the **cytoplasm** only. |
| Occurs in most organisms all the time. | Occurs in yeast, some bacteria, and muscles during hard exercise. |

$$\text{Aerobic: } C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O + \text{energy}$$
$$\text{Anaerobic (yeast): } C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2C_2H_5OH + 2CO_2 + \text{energy}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe an experiment to show that carbon dioxide is produced by a potted plant during respiration. *(13 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Aim:** to show that a living plant gives out carbon dioxide in respiration.

**Apparatus:** a potted plant, a large **bell jar** with a flat glass or wooden base, **black cloth/paper** (or a dark cupboard), **vaseline**, **lime water** (or hydrogencarbonate indicator) in two test tubes, a **U-tube or flask of soda lime (or potassium hydroxide solution)** to remove carbon dioxide from the incoming air, a **suction pump (aspirator)** and rubber tubing.

**Diagram to draw and label:** air is drawn in through the **soda lime / KOH flask**, then through a first **lime water tube** (to prove that the air is free of carbon dioxide: it stays clear), then into the **bell jar covering the potted plant** (sealed to the base with vaseline), and out of the jar through a second **lime water tube** connected to the **pump**. The whole jar is **covered with black cloth**.

**Procedure:**
1. Water the potted plant and cover the **soil and pot with polythene** so that the respiration of soil organisms is excluded.
2. Place the plant under the bell jar, seal the base with **vaseline** to make it airtight and **cover the jar with black cloth** (or put it in a dark place) so that **photosynthesis cannot take place** and no carbon dioxide is used.
3. Set up the apparatus as in the diagram and **pump air slowly** through the system for 1 to 2 hours.
4. Observe the lime water in the tubes.
5. **Control:** repeat with an identical jar containing the **pot and soil only (no plant)**, or with a dead plant.

**Observations:** the lime water in the **first tube (before the jar) remains clear**, showing the incoming air has no carbon dioxide. The lime water in the **tube after the jar turns milky (cloudy)**. In the control the lime water **stays clear**.

**Conclusion:** the carbon dioxide that turned the lime water milky was produced by the living plant, so **plants respire and give out carbon dioxide**.

**Precautions:** make the apparatus airtight; keep the plant in the dark so that photosynthesis does not use up the carbon dioxide; cover the soil; remove carbon dioxide from the incoming air; use the same conditions in the control.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the disadvantage of putting a potted plant inside a living room at night? *(2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown: At night there is **no light, so the plant does not photosynthesise** and does not release oxygen, but it **continues to respire**. It therefore **uses up oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide** in the closed room, competing with the people sleeping there. This **reduces the oxygen and increases the carbon dioxide** in the room, which may cause **headache, discomfort or suffocation** in a poorly ventilated room.
